subject: Workplace Skills
title: Learned Helplessness at Work
description: A quick win: understand Learned Helplessness at Work.

hook.text: Martin Seligman's dogs stopped trying to escape shock after learning their actions didn't matter. Humans do too.

buildup.text: When employees see that effort doesn't change outcomes, they stop trying. They sit in discomfort passively.

discovery.text: Learned helplessness explains why some teams give up on suggesting improvements after being ignored repeatedly.

twist.text: Small wins reverse it. One successful change can restart the belief that effort leads to results.

climax.text: If you feel helpless, pick the smallest possible action within your control and execute it. Agency rebuilds.

punchline.text: One small win breaks the helplessness cycle.

quiz.question: What causes learned helplessness in the workplace?
options: Lack of training and development opportunities
Repeatedly experiencing that effort doesn't change outcomes
